title: Judge the lesson, not only its items
statement: Passing items don't make a good set, lesson or course, so judge each whole on how its parts work together, taking item verdicts as given, never by adding them up.
example: One evaluator run rated 529 of 1026 items superior but 73 of 76 lessons inferior.
detail: One evaluator run over 76 cloned reading lessons rated 529 of their 1026 items superior but 73 of the 76 lessons inferior, and 65 of the 76 scored exactly 0 on not repeating themselves. The reading course passed its item-level evaluations but not the holistic course-level one, and a later project note says new metrics are needed to assess lesson sequencing. Judge their sequence, coverage, difficulty ramp and balance, with several lessons in view.
against: the scores are one run of a model judge, and the zeros on multi-passage lessons say more about how the evaluation was packaged than about the content. The lesson-level verdicts are the same evaluator's, not a person's, and the notes mark the figure internal-only (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`). At lesson level the evaluator does average item scores when there is no shared passage: '- _assemble_no_stimulus_result() returns item scores + avg overall' (shadow-bench, git commit 7b5da6e, line 9). The manual cover for cross-lesson defects is untested: 'assigned, not covered' (shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md line 147). The set specification does not count a shared format as repetition: "- Same question format (MCQ) applied to different concepts" (`icloud-work/incept/inceptbench/docs/MCQ_SET_PASS_SPEC.md`, line 203); these stems were near-copies, not one format applied to different concepts. Per-item verdicts vary between runs (see verdicts-vary), and the lesson rubric folds them in by threshold: a lesson fails factual accuracy only when more than 20% of its items do (`lesson_bundle/evaluation.txt` line 140), so a lesson with a few wrong items can pass, against the rule that a wrong key or wrong fact voids an item.

Finding: 57 checkable criteria have no coverage — 49 of them rejection-grade.

Root cause is structural. The evaluator's schema models a lesson as `passage + items[]` — no teaching steps, no vocabulary, no day/stage axis. So gradual release, opportunities to respond, reading architecture and vocabulary (63 criteria) are unreachable by construction.

Keep the latest user direction in view and audition the integrated experience rather than evaluating isolated components alone.
Item-level evaluation remains useful inside the process; the course contract supplies the upstream and cross-artifact evidence that isolated item evaluation does not test.
This is a pedagogical incompleteness, not a validator defect (all validators pass; no single validator spans vocab-to-you-do linkage).
